Reciprocal cross-species module conservation

Source: R/module_auroc.R
module_auroc_reciprocal.Rd

Runs module_auroc() in both directions, species 1 modules in the species-2 network and species 2 modules in the species-1 network, pairs the modules of the two species by reciprocal best hit on shared ortholog groups, and combines the two directions' p-values per pair.

module_auroc_reciprocal(
  modules1,
  modules2,
  net1,
  net2,
  orthologs,
  pval_combine = c("max", "min"),
  ...,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

modules1, modules2

Module maps over species-1 and species-2 genes (as_modules() or detect_modules()).

net1, net2

Network objects from compute_network().

orthologs

Ortholog pair table with Species1 (species-1 genes), Species2 and hog; swapped internally for the reverse direction.

pval_combine

"max" (both directions) or "min" (either).

...

Further arguments to module_auroc(), used in both directions (n_null, max_draws, n_cores, ...).

seed

Seed for both directions and the pi0 draws, or NULL for the ambient stream (package RNG contract).

Value

A data frame, one row per matched pair in species-1 module order: module1, module2, jaccard, p.val.1to2, p.val.2to1, p.val, q.val, z.1to2, z.2to1. Attributes unmatched (a list with species1 and species2: modules with no reciprocal partner, untested modules included) and resolution (pvalue_resolution() of p.val).

Details

Matching. Each module is reduced to the ortholog groups (hog) of its genes. Module \(a\) of species 1 and \(b\) of species 2 pair when \(b\) has the highest Jaccard index over groups with \(a\) among species-2 modules and \(a\) the highest with \(b\) among species-1 modules (ties go to the first module), the Jaccard is above 0, and both were tested by module_auroc(). module_correspondence() is not used: its Jaccard is over genes projected through a resolve_ortholog_map() map, one copy per group, while a module here is scored through every copy of its groups, so the overlap that matches the test is the overlap of groups.

Combination. pval_combine = "max" (default) takes pmax of the two directions: a pair counts as conserved only if each species' module holds in the other's network, the reciprocal criterion comparison_to_edges() applies to gene pairs (Netotea et al. 2014). pmax is a valid p-value for that intersection-union null. "min" accepts either direction and is not corrected for taking the smaller of two. The Storey pi0 behind q.val is estimated on the same combination of each direction's randomized p-value p.val.gt + U * p.val.eq, as in module_auroc().

References

Netotea, S., Sundell, D., Street, N. R. & Hvidsten, T. R. (2014). Evolution of the plant co-expression network. BMC Genomics, 15, 106. doi:10.1186/1471-2164-15-106
